items.name: Lion
items.description: The lion is a large carnivorous feline known as the king of the jungle. It has a distinctive mane that males develop as they mature. Lions live in prides consisting of related females and their offspring. They are apex predators, hunting cooperatively in groups. The roar of a lion can be heard from several kilometers away.

items.name: Tiger
items.description: Tigers are the largest cat species and are known for their striking orange coat with black stripes. They are solitary hunters, preferring to stalk prey alone. Tigers inhabit forests and grasslands across Asia. Each tiger has a unique pattern of stripes, like a fingerprint. They are endangered due to habitat loss and poaching.

items.name: Elephant
items.description: Elephants are the largest land animals, with long trunks and large ears. They use their trunks for drinking, eating, and communication. African elephants have larger ears than Asian ones. Elephants live in matriarchal herds led by the oldest female. They have excellent memory and can recognize other elephants after years.

items.name: Giraffe
items.description: Giraffes are the tallest mammals, with necks that can reach up to 6 feet long. Their long tongues help them eat leaves from tall trees. Giraffes have spotted coats that provide camouflage. They live in savannas and woodlands of Africa. Despite their height, giraffes can run at speeds up to 35 mph.

items.name: Zebra
items.description: Zebras are known for their black and white striped coats. Each zebra has a unique stripe pattern. They live in herds for protection against predators. Zebras communicate through vocalizations and body language. They inhabit grasslands and savannas in Africa.

items.name: Monkey
items.description: Monkeys are intelligent primates with opposable thumbs. They live in social groups and use tools in the wild. Different species inhabit various habitats from rainforests to mountains. Monkeys have expressive faces and communicate with gestures. Some monkeys, like capuchins, are known for their problem-solving abilities.

items.name: Panda
items.description: Giant pandas are bears native to China, known for their black and white fur. They spend most of their time eating bamboo. Pandas have a special wrist bone that acts like a thumb. They are solitary animals except during mating season. Conservation efforts have helped increase their population.

items.name: Kangaroo
items.description: Kangaroos are marsupials that hop on powerful hind legs. They carry their young in pouches called joeys. Kangaroos use their tails for balance while hopping. They are native to Australia and can jump up to 9 meters. Male kangaroos are called bucks, females does, and young joeys.

items.name: Koala
items.description: Koalas are tree-dwelling marsupials that sleep up to 20 hours a day. They feed almost exclusively on eucalyptus leaves. Koalas have strong limbs for climbing trees. They are native to Australia and are not bears despite their name. Koalas have a slow metabolism due to their low-energy diet.

items.name: Penguin
items.description: Penguins are flightless birds adapted for swimming. They have streamlined bodies and wings modified as flippers. Penguins live in colonies and breed in large groups. They are excellent swimmers, diving deep for food. Emperor penguins can hold their breath for up to 20 minutes.

items.name: Dolphin
items.description: Dolphins are highly intelligent marine mammals. They communicate using clicks and whistles. Dolphins live in pods and exhibit complex social behaviors. They use echolocation to navigate and find food. Dolphins can perform acrobatic jumps out of the water.

items.name: Shark
items.description: Sharks are cartilaginous fish with powerful jaws. They have been around for over 400 million years. Sharks have multiple rows of teeth that are constantly replaced. They play important roles in ocean ecosystems. Most sharks are not dangerous to humans.

items.name: Eagle
items.description: Eagles are large birds of prey with keen eyesight. They can spot prey from great distances. Eagles build large nests called aeries. They are symbols of strength and freedom in many cultures. Bald eagles are the national bird of the United States.

items.name: Owl
items.description: Owls are nocturnal birds with silent flight. They have excellent night vision and hearing. Owls can rotate their heads up to 270 degrees. They hunt small mammals and insects. Owls are found on every continent except Antarctica.

items.name: Snake
items.description: Snakes are legless reptiles that slither on their bellies. They use their tongues to sense their environment. Snakes shed their skin as they grow. Some snakes are venomous, while others constrict their prey. Snakes play important roles in controlling rodent populations.

items.name: Turtle
items.description: Turtles are reptiles with protective shells. They can live for over 100 years. Sea turtles migrate thousands of miles. Turtles lay eggs on beaches and return to the same spot. They have been around since the time of dinosaurs.

items.name: Frog
items.description: Frogs are amphibians that undergo metamorphosis. They start as tadpoles in water. Frogs have long tongues for catching insects. They absorb water through their skin. Frogs are indicators of environmental health.

items.name: Butterfly
items.description: Butterflies are insects that undergo complete metamorphosis. They start as caterpillars eating leaves. Butterflies have colorful wings covered in scales. They play important roles in pollination. Butterflies migrate long distances in some species.

items.name: Bee
items.description: Bees are social insects that live in colonies. Worker bees collect nectar and pollen. They communicate through dances to share food locations. Bees produce honey as food storage. They are crucial for pollinating many plants.

items.name: Ant
items.description: Ants are social insects living in complex colonies. They work together to find food and protect the nest. Ants communicate using pheromones. Some ants farm fungi for food. Army ants form massive swarms when hunting.
